Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old male lawyer with new-onset intermittent symptoms since a recent job change: headaches at work, palpitations, shortness of breath at rest, bilateral hand tingling, reduced appetite, unintentional 5 lb weight loss, and decreased libido. History of thyroid disease on thyroxine. Plan for in-person evaluation and thyroid labs.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Intermittent severe headaches; also palpitations, shortness of breath, bilateral hand tingling, reduced appetite, decreased libido.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began around the time of a job change (exact timing not stated). Occur at different times rather than simultaneously.
- Headache details:
  - Typically during work (meetings or on laptop); not on commute.
  - Location: predominantly frontal; does not radiate.
  - Associated symptoms: mild nausea; no prior history of frequent headaches before this period.
- Palpitations: Felt once daily or more; noted in the elevator in the morning as an example.
- Shortness of breath: Occurs while sitting at desk; not with exercise.
- Tingling: Bilateral hands; described as tingling/picking sensation; no leg involvement.
- Appetite/weight: Reduced appetite; unintentional 5 lb weight loss; no noticeable loosening of clothes and no external comments about weight change.
- Libido: Decreased since job change.
- Stress: Rates current work stress 7–8/10; reports law firm is usually high pressure.
- Pertinent negatives: Does not experience shortness of breath with exercise. No routine headaches before this period.
- Past medical history: Documented as “hyperthyroidism.” 
- Medications: Thyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Social history: Lawyer in London; alcohol about once weekly (a couple of glasses of wine); no smoking; denies recreational drug use.

Examination:
- Vitals: 
- Findings: 

Impression:
- Undifferentiated intermittent symptoms temporally associated with job change and increased stress: headaches, palpitations, shortness of breath at rest, bilateral hand tingling, reduced appetite with minor weight loss, and decreased libido.
- Known thyroid disease on thyroxine; further evaluation needed to assess thyroid status and cardiopulmonary causes.

Plan:
- Arrange in-person clinic appointment for physical examination, including cardiovascular and respiratory assessments.
- Order blood tests to assess thyroid function (per discussion: “blood tests for your thyroxine”).
- Defer starting medications until after in-person assessment and test results.
- Patient to book appointment via app; clinician will relay today’s history to colleagues to avoid repetition.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergy status; detailed medication list with doses/route/frequency; precise onset/timeline; neurological review beyond hand tingling; red flag headache screening (e.g., photophobia, focal deficits); family history; vitals and physical exam; mental health screening; sleep, caffeine use, hydration, and screen time history.
- Internal conflicts: PMH listed as “hyperthyroidism” while patient reports taking thyroxine (typically for hypothyroidism) — conflict noted.
- Other uncertainties: Initial triage noted “feeling hot,” but patient did not endorse; instead described episodic shortness of breath.
- Transcript quality: Some segments unclear/inaudible with interruptions; DOB incompletely stated.
